gloss.lead: Every word from the lessons, tagged with the unit it came from and paired with a short example that uses only words you have already met. Tap a word or a card to hear it. «Answers: hidden» at the top right covers the meanings so you can use these as flashcards. Below you can search or filter by unit.

review.setup_sub: Questions generated · tap to answer · missed words come back
review.lead: This review rests on three well-supported methods: retrieval practice (recalling beats re-reading, by a lot), interleaving (units mixed together rather than drilled in blocks), and immediate feedback with missed words returning until you get them right. A wrong answer costs you nothing — you just see the word once more.
review.need_more: Pick a scope first (at least 4 words)
review.note_body: What you learned most recently fades fastest, which is why the last two units are selected by default. After a few days, switch the scope to «All» for a random check. Mixed mode warms up with easy meaning questions before adding listening and recall.
review.fnote: Gapapa — no harm done. This word will come round again shortly.
review.praise_mid: Bagus! Most of it has stuck — clear up the few you missed.
review.praise_lo: Gapapa — run «missed words only» once more and it will come.
review.wrong_title: Worth another look (tap a card to hear it)

drill.setup_sub: Practise saying it, not just recognising it
drill.lead: Review mode checks that you know what a word means. This one trains answering on the spot — so that when a teacher asks where you are from, where you live, or what your name is, the answer arrives straight away. Questions are drawn at random, which pushes you to apply the pattern rather than memorise an answer.
drill.need_type: Choose at least one question type
drill.note_body: Fifteen questions here as a warm-up, then on to the vocabulary review, works well as a daily habit. Wrong answers cost nothing; anything you miss comes back once at the end of the round.
drill.cue_jam: How do you say this time?
drill.cue_angka: How do you read this number?
drill.why_jam: Remember: half past is «half of the next hour». 1:30 is setengah dua, not setengah satu.
drill.why_angka: Read it place by place: thousands, then hundreds, then tens — the same order as in English.
drill.why_other: Gapapa — this one comes back at the end of the round.
drill.praise_hi: Mantap banget! Quick off the mark
drill.praise_mid: Bagus! The shape is right — tidy up the misses.
drill.praise_lo: Gapapa — one more round of «missed questions only» and it will click.
